title: Cuajada with Blueberry Sauce
excerpt: Enjoy a Colombian classic with a unique twist: fresh cuajada (Colombian fresh cheese) served with a smooth homemade sauce of high-mountain blueberries. A traditional dessert, light and delicious.
imageAlt: A portion of fresh cuajada topped with warm whole-blueberry sauce, served on a traditional ceramic plate.
steps: Cut the cuajada into four portions or thick slices and place them on the serving plates at room temperature.
In a small pot over medium heat, combine the water with the grated panela and the cinnamon stick until the panela dissolves completely.
Add the Fresh Pick blueberries, grown in the high mountains of Guasca, along with the teaspoon of lemon juice.
Cook over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring gently with a wooden spoon so the berries release their natural juices without falling apart completely.
Remove the cinnamon stick and turn off the heat. Let the sauce rest for 3 minutes so it thickens slightly.
Spoon the warm blueberry sauce generously over each slice of cuajada and serve right away.
tips: If you like a contrast of temperatures, keep the cuajada cold in the fridge until the moment you pour the warm sauce over it.
To store Fresh Pick blueberries at home before cooking, keep them refrigerated in their original packaging without washing them until you are ready to eat them.
